(i) surface connectivity of flood plain pools homogenizes bacterial community composition and extracellular enzymic activity, whereas low connectivity leads to increased heterogeneity; (ii) hydrogeochemical parameters best explain variation of both bacterial community composition and activity, while the alga community and chromophore dissolved organic matter properties explain only minor fractions of variation.

1) surface connectivity homogenizes Bacterial Community Composition (BCC) and Extracellular Enzymatic Activity (EEA); 2) low connectivity increases BCC and EAA heterogeneity; 3) BCC and EAE are mainly explained by hydrogeochemical parameters and to a lesser extent by algae and chromophoric Dissolved Organic Carbon (cDOM) quality.
